components.gap: Durrett's variant of monotone convergence that replaces nonnegativity by an integrable negative part of the first function is absent from the current input route: Exercise 1.5.5 (p. 28: g_n increasing to g and int g_1^- dmu < infinity imply int g_n dmu increasing to int g dmu) and its expectation form Exercise 1.6.13 (p. 37: E X_1^- < infinity and X_n increasing to X imply E X_n increasing to E X). The route gives only the nonnegative theorem (integration-expectation.tex 81-90) and the counterexample r_n = -1_[n,infinity) showing that monotonicity alone fails (lines 260-262), never the source's sufficient lower-bound condition.

components.gap: The source's remark accompanying the definition of convergence in measure (p. 26) is not on the route for finite measure spaces: that on a space of finite measure convergence in measure is a weaker assumption than a.e. convergence (a.e. convergence implies convergence in measure), with bounded convergence proved in that greater generality. def:p15-lp-convergence (integration-expectation.tex 197-217) makes no comparison, and the only on-route implication is the probability-space case thm:p15-w02b-p15-013-as-probability(1) (limit-theorems-and-concentration-w02b-p15-013.tex 150-175), a narrowed variant (total mass one) of the source's finite-measure claim.

components.gap: (a) The source's presentation of the expectation form, Theorem 1.6.2 (p. 29), is incomplete on the route: the two-point illustration of the direction (P(X=x)=lambda, P(X=y)=1-lambda gives E phi(X) = lambda phi(x) + (1-lambda) phi(y) >= phi(EX)), Figure 1.6 (g(x) = x^2 - 3x + 3 with P(X=1) = P(X=3) = 1/2, p. 30) and the two named special cases |EX| <= E|X| and (EX)^2 <= E(X^2) as consequences of Jensen are absent (the two inequalities occur only separately, as the absolute-value bound of thm:p15-signed-integral-laws and the variance identity of thm:p15-expectation-bounds, not as Jensen's special cases). (b) The source's Jensen variants are absent: the equality case for strictly convex phi (Exercise 1.6.1, p. 35: phi(EX) = E phi(X) implies X = EX a.s.), Jensen for convex phi: R^n -> R (Exercise 1.6.2, p. 35) and the weighted arithmetic-geometric mean inequality from phi(x) = e^x (Exercise 1.6.12, p. 37).

components.gap: Durrett names Theorem 1.6.9 the change of variables formula and explains the name in its Remark (write h for X and P o h^-1 for mu: int_Omega f(h(omega)) dP = int_S f(y) d(P o h^-1)) (p. 32); he motivates it as the shift from (Omega,F,P) to a space where calculus can be done, usually S = R^d (p. 32), draws the consequence that expected values of functions of random variables are computed by integrals on the real line (p. 33), and states that the four-step sequence is a method for proving integration formulas, citing the proofs of Theorems 1.6.9 and 1.7.2 (p. 18), whose method 'will be used several times below' (p. 32). thm:p15-expectation-law-integral (integration-expectation.tex 324-348) and its proof (annex 405-459) carry neither the name, its explanation, nor these justificatory and methodological claims, and no on-route text names this identity the change of variables formula.

components.gap: (a) The Remark after Theorem 1.6.4 (p. 30) is only partly reflected: display (1.6.1), a^2 P(|X| >= a) <= EX^2 for phi(x) = x^2 and A = {|x| >= a}, is not stated, and the claim that some authors call the general result Markov's inequality and reserve Chebyshev's name for (1.6.1) is not given (the route names only the nonnegative-Y case 'Markov's bound' and the centred bound 'Chebyshev', integration-expectation.tex 359-375). (b) Display (1.6.3), var(X) <= EX^2 (p. 33), is not stated. (c) Exercises 1.6.3 (Chebyshev's bound is attained: for 0 < b <= a some X has EX^2 = b^2 and P(|X| >= a) = b^2/a^2; and is not sharp: a^2 P(|X| >= a)/EX^2 -> 0), 1.6.4(i) (the one-sided bound from phi(x) = (x+b)^2 for the two-point law, with equality), 1.6.5 (the two infima of tail probabilities under mean and variance constraints are 0) and 1.6.6 (P(Y > 0) >= (EY)^2/EY^2 by Cauchy-Schwarz) are absent from the route.

components.note: Every theorem of the chapter has an annex proof, and every pointer resolves on route to the promised content: product measures, exponential/gamma/normal moments (Examples 1.6.10-1.6.11), density representation, conditional L^p and L^2 results, interval/step/continuous approximation and Riemann-Lebesgue (Exercises 1.4.3-1.4.4), dyadic/truncation/small-set/simple approximation (1.4.2, 1.5.7, 1.5.9), essential bound/limit of norms/Minkowski/L^p (1.5.1-1.5.3), Poisson and geometric moments (1.6.13-1.6.14). Bernoulli Example 1.6.12 is on route at central-limit-theorems annex 537-539 though not pointed to. Unplaced exercises are recorded under the X- duty.

duties.duty: Durrett's 'Notation for special cases' after Theorem 1.4.7 (pp. 23-24): (a) int f(x) dx for int f dlambda on (R^d, R^d, lambda); (b) int_a^b f(x) dx for int_E f dlambda with E = [a,b]; (c) int f(x) dG(x) when mu((a,b]) = G(b) - G(a); (d) sum_{i in Omega} f(i) for counting measure on a countable Omega, with the remark that (d) shows results for sums follow from those for integrals.
duties.gap: Not established on the current input route: integration-expectation.tex fixes none of these conventions; the dG notation is fixed only for probability measures in def:p15-convolution-law (convolution-gamma-normal.tex 91-106); sums appear only as the countable atomic expectation formula for probability masses (integration-expectation.tex 344-347), not as integrals against counting measure with the source's remark; int f(x) dx and int_a^b f(x) dx are used across P15 without being defined as Lebesgue integrals.
